definition: Any failure originating in the propulsion system: engines, turbomachinery, feed, or motors.
example_events: Vanguard TV3 (1957); Nedelin catastrophe (1960); N1 (all 4 flights) (1969); Sea Launch Zenit-3SL (2007); Amos-5 / Zenit (SES) (2011); Antares Orb-3 (2014); Falcon 9 AMOS-6 (2016); Long March 5 Y2 (2017); Astra Rocket 3.3 LV0006 (2021); Firefly Alpha Flight 1 (2021); Astra TROPICS-1 (2022); ABL RS1 Flight 1 (2023); H3 TF1 (2023); Starship IFT-1 (2023); Peregrine Mission One (2024); Starship Flight 7 (2025); Starship Flight 8 (2025); PSLV-C61 / EOS-09 (2025); H3 (nav satellite) (2025); New Glenn static-fire explosion (LC-36) (2026)

definition: Unstable combustion or harmonic/structural-acoustic coupling that damages the engine or feed lines.
Failure of pumps, turbines, or rotating machinery feeding the engine.
Engine or stage fails to ignite or start correctly.
example_events: Nedelin catastrophe (1960); Astra Rocket 3.3 LV0006 (2021); H3 TF1 (2023)

definition: One or more engines shut down before commanded, degrading thrust.
example_events: N1 (all 4 flights) (1969); Astra Rocket 3.3 LV0006 (2021); Firefly Alpha Flight 1 (2021); Astra TROPICS-1 (2022); ABL RS1 Flight 1 (2023); Starship IFT-1 (2023); Starship Flight 8 (2025); H3 (nav satellite) (2025)

definition: Loss of tank pressure or feed integrity starving the engine of propellant.
example_events: Vanguard TV3 (1957); Amos-5 / Zenit (SES) (2011); Falcon 9 AMOS-6 (2016); New Glenn static-fire explosion (LC-36) (2026)

mode_name: Propellant / pressurant leak or line rupture
definition: Leak or rupture of a propellant, oxidizer, or pressurant line or tank.
Debris ingested into an engine causing failure.
Over- or under-pressure or case failure in a solid rocket motor.
Failure of load-bearing structure, seals, pressure vessels, or recovery hardware.
example_events: Soyuz 1 (1967); Challenger STS-51-L (1986); Columbia STS-107 (2003); Falcon 9 CRS-7 (2015); Falcon 9 AMOS-6 (2016); Vega VV15 (2019); SpaceX Starship Ship 36 (static fire) (2025)

definition: A joint or seal loses integrity, allowing hot gas or fluid escape.
Composite-overwrapped or metallic pressure vessel fails structurally.
example_events: Falcon 9 AMOS-6 (2016); SpaceX Starship Ship 36 (static fire) (2025)

definition: A structural member (strut, bracket, mount) fails below rated load.
Loss of thermal protection allows structural burn-through on ascent or reentry.
Buckling or thermo-structural failure of a tank dome or primary structure.
Parachutes or landing hardware fail to deploy or function.
Failure in flight software, avionics logic, sensors, or data configuration.
example_events: Ariane 5 Flight 501 (1996); Titan IV / Milstar (1999); Mars Polar Lander (1999); Schiaparelli EDM (2016)

definition: A numeric overflow or unhandled exception halts guidance or control software.
Software reused or specified outside its validated flight envelope.
A transient or spurious sensor reading is accepted as a valid event.
An incorrect constant, filter value, or data table is loaded into flight software.
Failure in attitude control, navigation, or state estimation.
example_events: Schiaparelli EDM (2016); Starship IFT-1 (2023); Starship IFT-3 (2024)

definition: Loss of attitude control from actuator, RCS, or thrust-vector failure.
Corrupted navigation state (e.g. IMU saturation) drives a wrong control action.
Failure of electrical power, distribution, or wiring.
example_events: Apollo 1 fire (1967); ABL RS1 Flight 1 (2023); H3 TF1 (2023)

definition: An electrical arc or short ignites a fire.
Loss or fault in power generation or distribution.
Failure during stage separation or fairing/payload separation.
example_events: Falcon 1 Flight 3 (2008); Soyuz MS-10 abort (2018); Firefly Alpha Flight 5 (Lockheed) (2024); Firefly Alpha FLTA006 (2025)

definition: Residual motion causes stages to recontact after separation.
Separation event damages hardware (e.g. nozzle) or fails to complete cleanly.
example_events: Soyuz MS-10 abort (2018); Firefly Alpha Flight 5 (Lockheed) (2024); Firefly Alpha FLTA006 (2025)

definition: Failure rooted in human action, process, or organizational decision-making.
example_events: Nedelin catastrophe (1960); Mars Climate Orbiter (1999); Proton-M / GLONASS (2013); Soyuz MS-10 abort (2018); New Glenn static-fire explosion (LC-36) (2026)

definition: A component is installed incorrectly (reversed, damaged, mislocated).
Inconsistent units or data conventions between teams cause a navigation or control error.
Unsafe ground operation or procedure violation causes a mishap.
example_events: Nedelin catastrophe (1960); New Glenn static-fire explosion (LC-36) (2026)

definition: Root cause not determined or not publicly released (cf. ICAO ADREP 'undetermined')
example_events: PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 (2026); Long March 3B/E (Shijian 32) (2026); Ceres-2 Y1 (maiden flight) (2026); KAIROS Flight 3 (2026); Tianlong-3 Y1 (maiden flight) (2026); New Glenn NG-3 (BlueBird 7) (2026); Long March 7A (ChinaSat-4B) (2026)

definition: Operator or agency has not published a root cause; the event cannot yet contribute a shareable lesson
example_events: PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 (2026); Long March 3B/E (Shijian 32) (2026); Ceres-2 Y1 (maiden flight) (2026); KAIROS Flight 3 (2026); Tianlong-3 Y1 (maiden flight) (2026); New Glenn NG-3 (BlueBird 7) (2026); Long March 7A (ChinaSat-4B) (2026)
